Here's some excellent news for anyone with a Switch or Switch 2: the Nintendo Black Friday deals are incredibly strong this year. Stronger than ever, really. Nintendo is known as a company that barely ever runs discounts, and when it does, they're pretty weak compared to other game makers. This year, though, retailers like Amazon and Walmart are taking the lead and dropping prices incredibly low. To wit: four digital Switch and Switch 2 games just dropped to $30 at Walmart. We're talking Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, and more. Let's take a look.

The games in question are the Nintendo Switch 2 games Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV, and the original Switch compilation Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2. That last one is a port of the 3D Mario classics from the Wii generation, if you can remember that far back.

All of these games are well worth the $30 price tag. Donkey Kong Bananza was made by the same team behind the stunning Switch platformer Super Mario Odyssey. We gave Donkey Kong Bananza a 10/10 score in our review, with critic Logan Plant writing, "Donkey Kong Bananza is a truly groundbreaking 3D platformer, with satisfying movement, powerful abilities, impressive destructible environments, and clever challenges that all come together in complete harmony to create Nintendo’s first Switch 2 masterpiece."

Kirby Air Riders, meanwhile, is an often-overlooked racer from the minds behind Super Smash Bros. Logan Plant gave it an 8/10 in our review, writing, "Kirby Air Riders' unconventional controls can get in its own way sometimes, but they don't stop it from being a fun, frantic action racing game with an almost unreal amount of stuff to do."

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV is a souped-up port of the 2024 Switch game. In our review, (once again) Logan Plant wrote, "Super Mario Party Jamboree itself is still fantastic, but the mixed new content of the Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV re-release adds frustrating limitations and strange design decisions to what was otherwise a polished, customizable experience." Still, for $30, it's well worth it.

And as for the Mario Galaxy collection? We didn't give it a straight-up review since mostly just direct ports of the Wii originals, but with controls that work better on Switch. It's a terrific pair of games that play great on Switch or Switch 2.

It's unclear how much digital stock Walmart has for these games. And at this Black Friday price, it's likely to go fast. So grab the games you want sooner than later.
